caveats: RSeQC infer_experiment is the method of record for strandedness and cannot run here: no aligned reads were provided. Any statement about strandedness from the count matrix alone is circumstantial.

A wrong strand setting applied uniformly to all six samples largely cancels in a within-gene between-group contrast; it inflates or deflates absolute counts but not the treated/control ratio. Say this rather than implying the DE result is unusable.
With 6 samples a PCA is unstable; read it as a picture, not as evidence of clusters.

If that reference is absent at run time, still run (a) and (c) and report the tissue check as not performed.

caveats: With 3 replicates per group the test has low power: both count models recover only a minority of true differences, mostly those with large fold changes. A gene absent from the significant list is not shown to be unchanged.

The strandedness caveat from T1S1 carries into every fold change reported here and must be restated, not dropped.
steps.context: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch, no covariates. Counts are gene-level integers from STAR/featureCounts keyed by gene symbol. RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so the power statement is computed in closed form.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between the 3 treated and the 3 control liver samples, at BH-adjusted p < 0.05, and which of them are called by both DESeq2 and edgeR?

grounding.reason: 3v3 unpaired fixed-effects counts from STAR/featureCounts: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001 and R-0009, minimal pre-filter per R-0002/R-0029, in-model median-of-ratios per R-0026 with the R-0147 GC/length diagnostic since cqn is absent, explicit reference level per R-0036, BH with independent filtering per R-0010/R-0043, and the low-power statement per R-0017/R-0162.

Pre-filter: >= 10 counts in >= 3 samples. Do not filter harder — independent filtering does the rest
Set the reference level of condition explicitly to control with relevel(); do not rely on alphabetical order
alpha = 0.05, BH adjustment, independent filtering on. Do not loosen alpha to compensate for the small design
Rank genes and draw plots on the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change; keep the unshrunken value and its standard error in the table
Select significant genes by padj only — never by unadjusted p-value and never by fold change alone
Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set; report the method-specific calls separately. Do not present the union as the result
Save the complete per-gene results table including the Wald stat column for the downstream enrichment step
steps.description: Import the raw integer counts as they are — no length correction, no tximport, no pre-scaling. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size). Set the condition factor's reference level explicitly to control. Fit DESeq2 with design ~ condition; median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model. Run the Wald test for the contrast (condition, treated, control) with alpha = 0.05, independent filtering on, BH adjustment. Inspect the histogram of unadjusted p-values before trusting the adjusted values and report its shape. Keep DESeq2's Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (with 3 replicates per cell it sets p and padj to NA rather than replacing counts) and report the number of NA p-values from outlier flagging separately from those the independent filter removed. Apply apeglm shrinkage to the coefficient for reporting and ranking, keeping the unshrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE in the table. Draw the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic: for each sample against the median sample, plot the log count ratio against gene GC content and against gene length; report any trend. cqn and EDASeq are not installed, so a trend is reported as a limitation, not corrected. Separately fit edgeR with TMM normalization and the quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design, and compute the overlap of the two significant sets. Before the model, state the expected power in closed form from n=3 per group, the observed depth, and a plausible biological coefficient of variation, naming the fold change detectable at 80% power. plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with strandedness audit
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 6 samples, CSV, gene symbols in the first column) from STAR/featureCounts on human liver, with metadata giving 3 treated and 3 control samples, unpaired, one batch. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control, and the user's stated doubt is that the strandedness of the library was never recorded, so the strand setting used at counting is unknown and the counts may be wrong.

That doubt is handled first, and honestly. The tool of record for strandedness (RSeQC infer_experiment) needs aligned reads, and no BAM/FASTQ exists in the inputs — only the summarised count matrix. So T1S1 runs the strandedness question as far as a count table permits: total assigned counts per sample, the detected-gene rate, the fraction of counts carried by the top genes, and a comparison of the per-sample expression profile against GTEx v8 liver median TPM. A count table produced with the wrong strand setting on a stranded library loses roughly half its reads and shows a depressed detection rate and a distorted liver profile; an unstranded setting applied to a stranded library inflates counts on antisense-overlapping loci. These are diagnostics, not a determination — the step reports what it can see and states plainly that the strandedness cannot be settled without the alignments. Critically, a strand error that is uniform across all six samples biases every sample the same way and therefore largely cancels in a within-gene, between-group contrast; a strand error that differs between samples does not, and would show as a split in the QC. T1S1 must say which of these the data looks like, because the credibility of the whole DE result depends on it.

T1S1 also does the standard structure QC on the same object: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition, to see whether the samples separate by treatment at all and whether any of the six departs from its group.

T1S2 is the differential expression itself: raw integer counts into DESeq2 with no length correction and no tximport (they are already gene-level counts), a minimal pre-filter of at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, design ~ condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, and the contrast named as condition, treated over control so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. The Wald test runs at alpha 0.05 with BH adjustment and independent filtering on, the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted, and apeglm shrinkage gives the fold changes used for ranking and plots while the unshrunken estimates stay in the table. Because STAR/featureCounts applies no bias model, the step also draws the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic (log count ratio of each sample against the median sample) — cqn and EDASeq are not installed, so if a trend appears the step reports it as a limitation rather than silently correcting. edgeR quasi-likelihood runs on the same counts and design as the second method; the intersection is the high-confidence set.

With 3 vs 3 there is very little power. Both count models recover only a minority of true differences at this replicate number, mostly large fold changes. The plan states the expected power before the model rather than after, keeps alpha at its default, and never loosens the threshold to manufacture a longer list. A gene absent from the significant list is not shown to be unchanged.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — every gene, not a thresholded subset — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties), and runs fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome and WikiPathways human as separate passes, each with its release stated and never merged. With 3 vs 3, the ranked test is the only defensible enrichment: an over-representation test on what will likely be a short significant list has no power.

T1S3 consolidates everything into a report with the power statement before the gene tables, the MA and dispersion plots, both fold-change columns with the standard error, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the leading-edge genes of each significant set, the GTEx liver tissue context for the top genes, and the full reproducibility record.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples

~ condition, reference level control, contrast condition treated vs control; expected power stated from closed form
DESeq2 Wald test, with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method for the overlap
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected

Consolidated report: power statement, MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading edge genes, reproducibility record

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with strandedness audit
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 6 samples, CSV, gene symbols in the first column) from STAR/featureCounts on human liver, with metadata giving 3 treated and 3 control samples, unpaired, one batch. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control, and the user's stated doubt is that the strandedness of the library was never recorded, so the strand setting used at counting is unknown and the counts may be wrong.

That doubt is handled first, and honestly. The tool of record for strandedness (RSeQC infer_experiment) needs aligned reads, and no BAM/FASTQ exists in the inputs — only the summarised count matrix. So T1S1 runs the strandedness question as far as a count table permits: total assigned counts per sample, the detected-gene rate, the fraction of counts carried by the top genes, and a comparison of the per-sample expression profile against GTEx v8 liver median TPM. A count table produced with the wrong strand setting on a stranded library loses roughly half its reads and shows a depressed detection rate and a distorted liver profile; an unstranded setting applied to a stranded library inflates counts on antisense-overlapping loci. These are diagnostics, not a determination — the step reports what it can see and states plainly that the strandedness cannot be settled without the alignments. Critically, a strand error that is uniform across all six samples biases every sample the same way and therefore largely cancels in a within-gene, between-group contrast; a strand error that differs between samples does not, and would show as a split in the QC. T1S1 must say which of these the data looks like, because the credibility of the whole DE result depends on it.

T1S1 also does the standard structure QC on the same object: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition, to see whether the samples separate by treatment at all and whether any of the six departs from its group.

T1S2 is the differential expression itself: raw integer counts into DESeq2 with no length correction and no tximport (they are already gene-level counts), a minimal pre-filter of at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, design ~ condition with control set explicitly as the reference level, and the contrast named as condition, treated over control so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. The Wald test runs at alpha 0.05 with BH adjustment and independent filtering on, the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted, and apeglm shrinkage gives the fold changes used for ranking and plots while the unshrunken estimates stay in the table. Because STAR/featureCounts applies no bias model, the step also draws the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic (log count ratio of each sample against the median sample) — cqn and EDASeq are not installed, so if a trend appears the step reports it as a limitation rather than silently correcting. edgeR quasi-likelihood runs on the same counts and design as the second method; the intersection is the high-confidence set.

With 3 vs 3 there is very little power. Both count models recover only a minority of true differences at this replicate number, mostly large fold changes. The plan states the expected power before the model rather than after, keeps alpha at its default, and never loosens the threshold to manufacture a longer list. A gene absent from the significant list is not shown to be unchanged.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — every gene, not a thresholded subset — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties), and runs fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome and WikiPathways human as separate passes, each with its release stated and never merged. With 3 vs 3, the ranked test is the only defensible enrichment: an over-representation test on what will likely be a short significant list has no power.

T1S3 consolidates everything into a report with the power statement before the gene tables, the MA and dispersion plots, both fold-change columns with the standard error, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the leading-edge genes of each significant set, the GTEx liver tissue context for the top genes, and the full reproducibility record.
